_meta.component: Supervision and the crash-loop breaker — nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md §12.2:616-618 ('Every process systemd-managed with restart policy. N restarts in M minutes ⇒ HALT + operator alert'). §12.11:777-778 puts the lifecycle verbs (`quarantine-restore`, `config-reload`) at supervision and resets this counter there.
_meta.authority: nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md §12A is the SEMANTIC authority for both knobs below. This file is the PHYSICAL layout only. Where the two disagree, §12A wins and this file is wrong.
_meta.role_separation: CONFIG-ROLE ONLY. Every value is a NUMBER; every word is under a `_`-prefixed documentation key that no loader reads.
_meta.lifecycle: §12.11 — boot-loaded, restart-only. Note the recursion and that it is not a problem: `config-reload` IS a supervised restart (§12.11:779), so supervision's own tunables change the same way every other module's do.
_meta.not_implemented_here: No supervision unit counts restarts today. These are homes for numbers.
_meta.no_cross_knob_rule: Stated rather than left to be noticed: these two knobs constrain NOTHING about each other that the spec fixes, so this file declares only the shared positivity rule. A cross-knob rule invented to make the file look better validated would be a rule with no authority behind it, which is the second-authority failure this whole directory is gated against.

_derivations.crash_loop_max: §12A:833 `CRASH_LOOP_MAX` = 3 restarts — stated outright. §4:272 is the rule for a strategy: 'after 3 restarts within a window (window = tunable variable), stop relaunching. The strategy is quarantined — left dead and flat, alert raised — while the rest of the system keeps trading.' §12.2:617 is the same breaker at process level.
_derivations.crash_loop_window_min: §12A:833 `CRASH_LOOP_WINDOW` — 'window over which they count. CC-calibrate.' §4:272 explicitly leaves it a tunable variable and §12.2:617 spells the rule 'N restarts in M minutes', so the unit is minutes. 10 is a placeholder.

_boot_validation.why: Both knobs must be > 0. §12A:801-802 requires boot validation to reject an invalid set; a zero restart cap quarantines a strategy on its first crash, and a zero window means no two restarts ever fall in the same window, so the breaker never trips.
